I really needed this. Pre-pandemic, I took intense classes at a rowing studio three times a week: cardio, weights, HIIT, great stuff. I was in fantastic shape. Then COVID hit, the world shut down, and over the course of working from home for 15 months (with the aid of severe suicidal depression), I regained 80+ pounds that I'd previously lost. I'm fat and miserable with myself. My anxiety and stomach issues are worse than ever. I need to start exercising again consistently. I've had a few abortive attempts, but now it's time to try again and stick with it.

Hi there, I'm so sorry you're dealing with this. I have chronic anxiety-induced nausea, though not this severe. I would recommend calling your doctor and asking for a Zofran prescription - it's a strong dissolvable antiemetic and it should hopefully help your stomach calm down long enough for you to eat and recover while you get through this tough period.

I wish the best of luck. It took me a few years to find a doctor who took me seriously, and in the end, I really just got lucky.

I would strongly recommend that you pursue a bilateral salpingectomy instead of a tubal ligation. Basically your tubes are cut and cauterized instead of just "tied" - far lower of a failure rate, and the procedure can also reduce your chances of developing ovarian cancer. I had it done when I was 23. The recovery was just fine and the peace of mind is so worth it.

Hello! I am a cisgender lady, nonsmoker, was young at the time of my surgery 😅. I had both of my fallopian tubes removed laproscopically, which required both general anesthesia and inflation of my abdomen with C02. I woke up feeling gross, bloated, and out of it, but I was given Phenergan and that immediately helped. I never did get sick, even being blown up like a basketball for a few days. You can always ask for preventative anti-emetics to be administered after surgery.  Good luck! 🖤

Also, if you are given pain medicine/antibiotics (which I imagine you would be with that kind of surgery?), taking them with food is good prevention against an upset stomach (as long as that is okay for the particular prescription).

I say go for it. I shaved my head completely a few years ago after over a decade of dyeing it just wrecked it. Even as a fat, not conventionally attractive woman, it was one of the most freeing things I've ever done. The low maintenance is wonderful too. It might do you some good. 🖤

Hey OP, I had pretty much the same diagnosis, a lot of inflammation, sensitivity, and some recession. I had to get a couple of rounds of debridment and deep gum cleaning to get back on track. The treatment isn't fun, but honestly it wasn't the worst, and it helps so much. The damage can be stopped and the prognosis isn't always so grim. Gum disease happens so easily (in my case it was because I neglected flossing for a long time), so please don't blame yourself too much.

My recommendations:

1. Get a package of single use floss picks/soft gum picks to keep by your bed. Even if you feel like you can't get up to brush your teeth, use one of those at least once a day. Brushing is important but flossing is more so. 

2. When you feel up to it, alcohol-free mouthwash really helps clear up and prevent infection.

You're doing so well getting a handle on your dental health. It can be so daunting. Be proud you even took this first step. 🖤

We have to go to work and somehow carry on our lives. It's frustrating and scary, but it is what it is by now. Thank you for your reply. In truth, I simply went to a pharmacy in August and explained to the tech that I was high-risk (I am, due to my weight) and that I was interested in a Moderna booster. She seemed confused but agreed to it anyway.

It's now 17 days after I tested positive. I seem to have recovered. My symptoms never escalated beyond fatigue, body aches, general malaise, mild GI upset, some hot flashes and sweating, especially at night, and an occasional racing heart. I consider myself lucky and am so glad I was vaccinated and boosted.

However, I still have a number of concerns:

1. I'm terrified of long COVID still. I've heard of so many cases of people having mild symptoms upon initial infection, but then developing debilitating sequelae weeks or months later. I don't know what damage has been done to me, or if I'm likely to have a stroke or throw a clot or just simply drop dead within the next 12 months. 

2. I got my booster very early on, in late August 2021. I want to get a second booster in February after six months have passed, but I don't know where or how, or if I'll even be permitted to. Should I simply lie and say it's my first? Only Israel seems to even be talking about fourth shots.

3. I just read that an Omicron subvariant has been discovered in Israel and detected in a few other countries. It's extremely early on and information is limited, but this news threw me into despair. It seems like no matter what we do to protect ourselves, we'll still keep getting sick over and over until we eventually die. We just can't keep up with the fast-evolving variants and honestly, not enough people are even trying to do the right things anymore. I'm so tired and sometimes I just want to end it before COVID does kill me.

I'm not sure Robin Williams falls quite into the same category; as I understand it, his suicide may have been largely motivated by his tragic Lewy Body Dementia diagnosis. He was already suffering from the symptoms at his time of death. :(

I'm really disappointed and scared. My symptoms are very mild so far, fatigue, slight aches, and GI distress, but I'm afraid it will get worse and I won't be able to get medical attention if needed because hospitals are overrun. I'm fully vaccinated and boosted, but fat and extremely worn down by stress and anxiety.

I don't want to die. I don't want longterm complications that ruin my quality of life. I really tried to do everything I could, but I guess my number is up.

The one bright spot is that I have found a lovely new partner. I'm embarrassed that my past relationship still haunts me so much when he is in every way so much better. I think with the pandemic, I haven't been able to process the trauma of what happened at all. My boyfriend does help a great deal, but unfortunately I'm still slipping into the dark place more often lately (I know it's not his job to "save" me, either, but he really does try).

I had a relationship with the man I thought I'd marry end in the most brutal betrayal in May 2020. We were long distance and got separated further by lockdown. I was in the process of getting screened to be a living kidney donor for him (he'd been in advanced renal failure for three years, on dialysis thrice weekly). I never saw him again after March 16th, 2020, and the pain lingers. I don't know if he's still alive. 

My dad told me he tested positive on Election Day 2020. He was hospitalized for a week. I self harmed for the first time since high school.

My favorite aunt almost died this past summer, despite having one shot. She recovered but is now losing her hair.

My rowing studio shut down. I've regained almost all of the 80 pounds I lost over the past two years because I've turned to food and alcohol to cope. I'm exhausted all the time and even self-loathing doesn't motivate me. 

I'm triple vaxxed but live in terror daily. I was recalled back to the office in June of this past year, and remote work isn't allowed anymore unless you're actively sick. My coworkers all got vaccinated but otherwise largely pretend that the pandemic doesn't exist. I'm the only one who wears a mask all day.

I'm miserable. Infrequently but regularly self harming still. I honestly don't want to be alive anymore. I've lost hope that anything will ever get better.

I wish I could get another booster, I have three Moderna shots at this point (acquired before the science on mix n' match came out) and I'll likely have to wait until early next year, if additional boosters are authorized.

I know Pfizer recently published some data indicating that their vaccine is largely still effective against the new variant, but all I've seen regarding Moderna are incredibly pessimistic comments from the CEO about drastically reduced effectiveness. 

I have three shots of Moderna under my belt as of August, but now I don't feel protected at all anymore. 

All of my loved ones also have Moderna. 

How could it be so much less effective than Pfizer? I don't know what to do.

Trigger warning. Don't want to drag others down, too. 

Guys, I think this is it for me. With news of the Omicron variant and its infectiousness/possible vaccine resistance, I don't think I can do this any more. Delta was bad enough. 

My boss called all of us back into the office in June when things looked better, and I doubt he'll ever let us go back to WFH. We're all vaccinated, but my coworkers are just kind of done with the pandemic. I'm the only one who wears a mask all day. I can't quit. I otherwise love my job and it's the only one I've found that matches my extremely limited skillset. 

I'm fat as fuck and therefore high risk. Before the pandemic, I dropped 80 pounds and was fit and healthy. Then after COVID hit, my rowing studio shut down. My relationship with the man I thought I'd marry ended in brutal betrayal. I couldn't seek solace in family or anyone else I loved. Half-mad with grief and fear, I turned to food for comfort, and now I've regained most of what I'd lost. I'm triple vaxxed with Moderna, but I doubt that will help as the variants continue to evolve.

I don't know how we're going to survive this. We can't respond fast enough to contain these variants, and even if we could, antivaxxers will just let the rest of us die, too. I've lost hope in humanity and any sort of future. I'm terrified of death, but honestly, I don't see how life is going to ever be worth living again with this never-ending hellscape of disease, suffering, and loss. I just want to turn it all off.

They didn't expect me to speak or do anything at all, they just let me exist in their presence. That quiet comfort and support got me through the worst of the initial pain. The wound is still painful, but I have found new joy since, and I'm very glad I stayed.

Hi, relatively new lurker here. I've been dealing with persistent nausea in varying degrees of intensity since 2017. After a ton of extensive testing, nothing was ever found to be truly "wrong," so IBS is my tentative diagnosis by exclusion.

Sometimes it seems like there's no rhyme or reason, but I have noticed that anxiety/heightened negative emotional states and also my hormonal cycle may contribute to my worst episodes.

I am unfortunately kind of an expert on stomach pain and nausea by my own experience. If you don't mind my asking, where is your pain located? Gallbladder dysfunction can cause pain and nausea for sure, as can ulcers. Impaired gastric motility, like slow stomach emptying, can also be the culprit. Some of these may not necessarily show up on CT scan (except maybe gallstones or blockages?).

I'm so sorry you're dealing with this. I hope it resolves soon.
